'''Meir Lahav''' ({{langx|he|מאיר להב}}; born 1936 in [[Sofia]], Bulgaria) is an Israeli chemist and materials scientist. He is an emeritus professor at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Faculty – materials|periodical=Weizmann.ac.il|publisher=|url=http://www.weizmann.ac.il/materials/faculty-and-staff/faculty|format=|access-date=2017-09-02|last=|date=|year=|language=en|pages=|quote=}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Lahav emigrated to Israel in 1948. He studied at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], where he obtained a master's degree in [[polymer chemistry]] in 1962. With Gerhard Schmidt at the Weizmann Institute of Science, he obtained a Ph.D. in solid state chemistry. As a postdoctoral fellow, Lahav worked with [[Paul Doughty Bartlett]] at [[Harvard University]], among others, before returning to Israel in 1971. Since 1985 he has held a full professorship at the Weizmann Institute.

In a long-term collaboration with [[Leslie Leiserowitz]], Lahav dealt with how crystal formation and growth can be influenced by targeted impurities (useful impurities) and with the direct determination of the sense of chirality of molecules. He investigated crystallization and interface phenomena such as the packing of amphiphilic molecules at the phase boundary and the basis for heterogeneous catalysis. He sought to understand biomembranes and designed self-assembling Langmuir-Blodgett layers (see self-assembling monolayer), investigated reaction pathways through asymmetric transformations into chiral and centrosymmetric crystals, guest-host interactions in organic solids, the correlation of macroscopic phenomena with molecular chirality, as well as stereochemical and regiospecific photoreactions within organic solids.

Lahav received the Centenary Prize of the Royal Society of Chemistry in 1984/85,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Centenary Prizes for Chemistry and Communication - previous winners |url=https://www.rsc.org/prizes-funding/prizes/find-a-prize/centenary-prizes/previous-winners/ |access-date=2023-10-13 |website=Royal Society of Chemistry |language=en-GB}}</ref> the Prelog Medal in 1987,<ref>[https://chab.ethz.ch/forschung/institute-und-laboratorien/LOC/prelog-lecture/fruehere-prelog-lektoren.html Prelog-Lektoren und deren Laudatien]{{Archive url|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200716235831/https://chab.ethz.ch/forschung/institute-und-laboratorien/LOC/prelog-lecture/fruehere-prelog-lektoren.html|date=2020-07-16}}</ref> the [[Gregori Aminoff Prize]] in 2002,<ref>{{cite web|title=Kungl. Vetenskapsakademien|periodical=Kva.se|publisher=|url=http://www.kva.se/en/priser/pristagare/meir-lahav-2|format=|access-date=2017-09-02|last=|date=|year=|language=|pages=|quote=}}</ref> the [[Chirality Medal]] in 2006,<ref>{{cite journal|title=Chirality|website=onlinelibrary.wiley.com|publisher=|url=http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/journal/10.1002/(ISSN)1520-636X|format=|access-date=2017-09-02|last=|date=|year=|language=en|pages=|doi=10.1002/(ISSN)1520-636X|quote=|doi-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and the [[Israel Prize]] in 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Weizmann professors claim Israel Prize in chemistry and physics|website=haaretz.com|publisher=|url=https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2016-02-07/ty-article/.premium/weizmann-profs-claim-israel-prize-in-chemistry-and-physics/0000017f-e13b-d568-ad7f-f37b83bd0000|format=|access-date=2017-09-02|last=|date=2016-02-07|language=|pages=|quote=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Israel Prize Winners |url=https://www.jewishvirtuallibrary.org/israel-prize-winners |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=www.jewishvirtuallibrary.org}}</ref> For 2018 he was awarded the [[The EMET Prize for Art, Science and Culture|EMET Prize]].<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20180730081018/http://www.emetprize.org/ EMET Prize 2018]}} (in Hebrew)</ref> In 2021 he and [[Leslie Leiserowitz]] jointly received the [[Wolf Prize in Chemistry]].<ref>[https://wolffund.org.il/2021/02/09/meir-lahav/ Wolf Prize in Chemistry 2021]</ref> He has been a member of the Leopoldina since 1997.<ref name="b607">{{cite web | title=Mitglieder | website=Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften Leopoldina | date=29 June 2023 | url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/meir-lahav/ | language=de | access-date=9 March 2025}}</ref>

Meir Lahav is married and has three children.
